page_title: Tracexy — Trace the failure back to the app.

sources.entry: Tracexy - Open-source, session-based network intelligence for capturing live traffic and investigating PCAP/PCAPNG files locally. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/RockxyApp/Tracexy) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Tracexy
summary.one_liner: Tracexy is a native, open-source (AGPL-3.0) macOS packet analyzer that traces live traffic and PCAP/PCAPNG captures from the app to the session to the exact packet, keeping data local by default.
use_cases: Investigating why a Mac app's network connection failed
Opening and analyzing saved PCAP or PCAPNG captures on a Mac
Attributing network sessions to the app or process that created them
Inspecting HTTP/2, WebSocket, RTP/SIP or SMB2 traffic in captures
Preparing reviewed evidence and reports for handoff
summary.what_it_does: Tracexy captures live traffic from a chosen Mac interface, with BPF filters and bounded packet retention, or opens existing PCAP and PCAPNG files. It groups traffic into sessions and attributes supported sessions to Mac processes, showing application, destination, DNS name, protocol and timing. Users can narrow views by app, domain, IP, or protocol, and move from overview and I/O graphs to decoded Ethernet/IP/transport/application layers and raw hex for individual packets. The page also describes DNS, TCP/UDP, TLS and QUIC metadata inspection, cleartext HTTP/2 and WebSocket following, RTP/SIP and SMB2 object evidence, and Findings linked to source frames.
notable: Session-first, app-aware design that links processes to packets, unlike packet-first tools
Open-source under AGPL-3.0 with a notarized macOS download
Local-by-default: packet data is not uploaded automatically; offline GeoIP/ASN lookup
Free Community tier with a one-time Pro license (from $18 founding price) adding comparison, scheduling, reports and TLS key-log launcher
caveats: Pro features (cross-capture comparison, scheduled capture, reports, redaction profiles) require a paid license; Team and Enterprise tiers are roadmap only
Encrypted HTTP/2 and WebSocket (h2, wss) payloads are not decoded; decryption only works with operator-supplied key material for supported captures
Page reports a planned Product Hunt launch on 24 November 2026; Homebrew availability was requested by users but not confirmed on the page
